title: Exploring villages and cities
summary: Learn to tell rural and urban places apart.
keyIdeas: Rural municipalities usually have fewer residents and more farmland.
Cities usually have more residents, buildings and services.
The council organises public services in each municipality.

basicKnowledge: C. Sociedades y territorios › Alfabetización cívica
C. Sociedades y territorios › Conciencia ecosocial

activities.prompt: Where are we most likely to find skyscrapers and heavy traffic?
activities.explanation: Large cities often have very tall buildings and many vehicles.
activities.hint: Think of a place where many people live.

activities.prompt: Villages usually have fewer residents than cities.
activities.explanation: Villages usually have smaller populations, while cities have many more residents.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about municipal government.
activities.explanation: The mayor leads the council together with councillors.
activities.sentence: The person who leads the council is the ___.

activities.prompt: Sort these features by where they are more common.
activities.explanation: Farmland is more common in rural areas. Underground trains and skyscrapers are found in some large cities. Not all places are alike.

items.text: Low family houses with vegetable gardens

activities.prompt: Match each local service to its main job.
activities.explanation: These services help residents. One or more councils, or other public authorities, may organise them.

pairs.right: Sweeping streets and emptying litter bins
Putting out fires and rescuing people

activities.prompt: Few cars pass along Omar's street, but many pass along Nerea's. Why is Omar's street usually quieter?
activities.explanation: In this comparison, fewer vehicles make less traffic noise. Not all villages and cities have the same noise levels.
activities.hint: Look at how many cars pass.
options: Villages have no paths or people
Fewer cars and lorries pass along it

activities.prompt: Put these places in order from fewest to most residents.
activities.explanation: In these examples, a tiny village has few residents, a medium-sized town has more, and a large city has many more.

activities.prompt: Read carefully and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Villages and cities can offer different ways to travel each day.
activities.title: Two close cousins
activities.text: Aisha lives in a quiet village. She cycles to school every day. Her cousin Hugo lives in a large city. He takes the underground train to school. They visit each other during the holidays and play together.

questions.prompt: How does Aisha get to school?
questions.explanation: Aisha cycles to school every day.

questions.prompt: Which public transport does Hugo use?
questions.explanation: Hugo uses an underground train, found in some large cities.

activities.prompt: Many cars together produce exhaust fumes. How can we improve city air?
activities.explanation: Cycling produces no exhaust fumes, and buses can carry many people using fewer vehicles.
activities.hint: Look for an option that uses fewer petrol engines.
options: Travel alone in our own cars
Remove all the trees from pavements

activities.prompt: Sort these jobs by where they are more common.
activities.explanation: Farming and livestock work are common in rural areas. Many services are concentrated in cities.

items.text: Drive a tram along an avenue
Harvest olives in an olive grove
Work in a large department store
